messages:
Anya Patel: Hey team — quick sync on the PRD checklist for Dedicated launch. We need a tight, customer-facing set of launch gates around SLAs, autoscale behavior, and graceful degradation.
Ben Liu: +1. Can we call out exact SLO numbers and what counts as a breach?
Sofia Martinez: Draft suggestion: p95 latency <= 120ms for small gen (<=128 tokens), error rate < 0.3% for committed pools, throughput target X qps/node. We should define recovery windows and whether transient blips count.
Raj (EngSRE): For recovery windows: recommend 15m sustained breach triggers an incident, 5m sustained for autoscale to add capacity. Hysteresis on scale down should be 10m to avoid flapping.
Marta (Product): Customers asked for "no surprise" behavior — we need explicit fallback rules: if Dedicated pool capacity exhausted, route to compatible lower-cost model only with customer opt-in; otherwise queue or rate-limit.
Anya Patel: Agree. Acceptance criteria idea: 1) Load test shows 95% of requests meet p95 under committed traffic +40% burst for 30m, 2) Autoscale adds X nodes within T seconds under linear ramp, 3) Rollback playbook validated.
Ben Liu: For autoscale SLA, we should quantify: under a 3x traffic spike over baseline, we should increase throughput capacity by 2.5x within 3 minutes for warm nodes, 8-10 minutes for cold starts. Document warm vs cold assumptions.
Sofia Martinez: Edge cases: noisy neighbors causing CPU/PCIe contention, KV cache pressure on long-context workloads, and model-quantization fallbacks that alter latency profiles. Call these out and provide mitigation.
Raj (EngSRE): Ops checklist additions: synthetic telemetry route, canary ramp with socket-level metrics, automated rollback if p99 > 1s for 5m in canary. Also add circuit-breaker that gates downstream router when queue depth > threshold.
Marta (Product): Customer acceptance tests should include: 1) their representative prompt set hitting our cluster, 2) runbook walkthrough, 3) agreed fallback policy. Need sign-off from customer success.
Anya Patel: Example SLO fragment to include in PRD:
```
- SLA: 99.5% availability for committed pool (monthly)
- Performance SLO: p95 <= 120ms for small gen under committed baseline
- Degradation mode: if <= 95% of committed capacity available, automatically notify and apply burst policy (configured per contract)
```
Ben Liu: We should also list measurable KPIs for launch: mean token throughput per GPU, cost per 1M tokens, transient error counts, time-to-scale. Those map back to pricing and capacity commitments.
Sofia Martinez: Can we add a short acceptance-run playbook with phases: unit tests -> perf lab -> canary with 1 customer -> private preview -> GA. Each phase has clear go/no-go gating.
Raj (EngSRE): On rollback triggers: p95 regression >20% vs baseline for 10m, error rate doubling, sustained OOMs. Add a manual abort path plus automated partial rollback to warm fallback model.
Marta (Product): I'll synthesize into the PRD. @autoscale-bot can you attach the most recent autoscale latency curves from last perf run? :thumbsup:
autoscale-bot: Attached: perf-run-2026-03-12.csv (summary)
Anya Patel: Thanks. Action items: Marta to update PRD with explicit SLOs and acceptance checklist; Raj to draft ops runbook and rollback playbook; Ben to add throughput/cost KPIs and scaling latency targets; Sofia to enumerate edge-case testcases. We aim to lock PRD for review by next Tue.
Ben Liu: Noted. Will add the numeric throughput targets and a short comms blurb for customers.
Sofia Martinez: I'll add the test matrix.
Raj (EngSRE): Scheduling a tabletop for rollbacks Friday.
Marta (Product): Great — ping me drafts in this thread. :raised_hands:
